newsitem.title: USA: SEC accuses 3 ministers of bilking church members.
newsitem.headline: SEC accuses 3 ministers of bilking church members.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Monday it has filed a civil complaint against three ministers alleging they bilked some 200 investors in 16 states, including church members, out of $3.5 million through a ponzi scheme.

In its complaint filed on July 15 in a federal court in Louisiana, the SEC alleged Wendell Rogers, Donald Hammond and Willis Davis, between 1993 and 1994 operated a ponzi scheme by selling shares in a sham Jonesville, La, company called Sunbelt Development Corp.
"The defendants promised exorbitant returns on investments along with the return of the investors' principal when, in fact, Sunbelt was actually operating a ponzi scheme," the SEC said.

In its complaint, the SEC alleged the defendants told potential investors Sunbelt would invest their money in Cedar Hill Game Call Co, a small maker of game calls and equipment used by hunters when only $20,000 of the funds collected went toward that investment.
Investors were told they would earn returns of 60 percent to 100 percent each year until Cedar Hill went public, according to the SEC's complaint.
The agency further charged that investors were told Sunbelt made short term loans to doctors and lawyers willing to pay high interest rates.
"Many of those who took advantage of this investment opportunity were elderly and retired," the agency alleged.
The SEC said it is trying to seek forfeiture of the alleged illegal profits of the three men and any civil penalties.
None of the defendants could be reached for comment and an SEC official handling the case did not know of any attorneys representing the three men.
